title: MapleStory Classic Crossbowman Build and Leveling Guide: Lv 30-70
intro: Crossbowmen trade attack speed for heavier damage. Iron Arrow pierces through up to four mobs, Crossbow Mastery can ignore enemy's physical defense, and Final Attack gives a strong single-target follow-up.

blocks.p: This guide is based off of a realistic lv 70 Crossbowman build by Grummash.
**Pros**

ul: #6 AoE damage and #4 Damage/MP at level 70 in the current benchmark.
Iron Arrow pierces four mobs in front of you.
Crossbow Mastery can ignore enemy Weapon Defense on 20% of attacks.
The level 50-70 crossbows in this guide carry more base W.ATK than the matching bows.
Soul Arrow lets you shoot without using up arrows.

blocks.p: **Cons**

ul: Crossbows attack slower than bows, even with Booster.
Iron Arrow loses 20% damage on each later mob it pierces.
Inside 65 px your crossbow whacks instead of firing. It is a weak melee swing.
The best maps need long, flat lanes that keep mobs lined up.
No movement skill in second job. You walk and jump to every platform.

blocks.p: This guide continues from the Bowman level 1 to 30 guide. Its no-reset endpoint is Arrow Blow 20, Critical Shot 15, The Eye of Amazon 15, Focus 10, and Power Knockback 1.

Grummash's saved level 70 build uses Double Shot 20, Arrow Blow 1, and Focus 9. If you want that exact endpoint, move 19 SP from Arrow Blow and 1 from Focus into Double Shot. The live Cash Shop price for this reset is unconfirmed.
Keep Henesys citizenship from the first-job guide. Its rewards cover arrows, Accuracy consumables, DEX options, and weapon scrolls for both Bowman branches.
A training map only works when your attacks connect. Every miss spends MP, wastes the attack animation, and lowers EXP per minute.

blocks.h2: Levels 30-70: Crossbowman skill build and leveling

ol: Start the second-job advancement by talking to Athena Pierce in Henesys.
Deliver her letter to the instructor on The Road to the Dungeon and enter the test.
Collect 30 Dark Marbles from the test mobs to receive The Proof of a Hero.
Bring the proof back to Athena and select Crossbowman.

blocks.p: Second-job SP cannot be spent on first-job skills, so finish the first-job plan by level 30. Character Builder flags any build that breaks it.

blocks.note: **Why Mastery and Booster come first:** At level 35, this sample build improved from about 5,207 to 7,284 Advisor EXP/min. At level 40, it improved from 8,369 to 9,712 EXP/min. Stronger low rolls and faster attacks become much more valuable before Iron Arrow is maxed.

blocks.h3: Possible changes to the default order

blocks.p: Max Iron Arrow immediately when your map keeps four mobs lined up and they already die cleanly. You give up early Mastery, Booster, and Soul Arrow.
If MP is your limit against single targets, move Final Attack ahead of the Booster and Soul Arrow levels. It barely changes Double Shot damage, but it costs no MP.

This continues from the crossbow path in the Bowman guide: 20 base STR and 142 base DEX. Every crossbow from Heckler to Gross Jaeger needs STR equal to its level minus 10, so 1 STR per level keeps each one wearable on time. Gross Jaeger requires 60 STR, ten less than Golden Hinkel, so those ten AP stay in DEX.

Crossbows use both hands, so Crossbowmen cannot equip shields. Carry arrow stacks until Soul Arrow lasts long enough for full training sessions. While Soul Arrow is active, attacks do not consume arrows.

blocks.h2: W.ATK or Critical Rate on gloves?

blocks.p: These numbers use Grummash's realistic level 70 Crossbowman build and five successful Lesser glove scrolls. Both options use the same five slots.

**+5 W.ATK**
102 to 107 total W.ATK
About 4.9% more expected damage.

**+5% Critical Rate**
29% to 34% Critical Rate
About 1.83% more expected damage.

blocks.note: **Pick Attack.** The five-scroll Attack setup deals about 3.01% more expected damage than the Critical Rate setup on this build.

blocks.p: Critical Shot raises this build to 41% Critical Damage. This is one of the closer comparisons, but W.ATK still wins at level 70.

**The ratio is the same at every grade.** Lesser gives +1 W.ATK or +1% Critical Rate (+2 M.ATK), Intermediate +2/+2% (+4 M.ATK), Greater +3/+3% (+6 M.ATK), and Chaos +4/+4% (+8 M.ATK). Matching grades have the same success and destruction rates.

**W.ATK also helps guaranteed kills.** It raises every physical hit, including your weakest normal roll and every critical hit. Critical Rate changes how often a critical occurs, so it cannot improve the weakest non-critical roll.

blocks.h2: Example builds and Training Advisor maps

blocks.p: The Advisor checks the weakest normal hit. Average damage does not decide a guaranteed kill. A guaranteed two-attack result means two bad damage rolls still kill the mob and Accuracy is high enough to prevent misses. Each pick shows Danger and the nearest potion and arrow refill. Crossbowmen also need the lane to cooperate: Iron Arrow's later targets must stay lined up in front.

blocks.p: **Before you settle in:** The Iron Arrow picks from level 40 on assume every Iron Arrow pierces all four mobs. Watch the last mob Iron Arrow pierces. If it needs another Iron Arrow after the first mob dies, include that extra shot when comparing maps. Flat ground and a clean firing lane can beat a higher-ranked map with broken platforms.
Iron Arrow pierces up to four mobs. The first takes 100% of the calculated damage, followed by 80%, 60%, and 40%. A dense horizontal lane gets the full value; staggered platforms do not.
**At level 70, the benchmark deals about 5,852 expected total damage across four targets.**

Max Mastery raises the minimum damage roll to Mastery 10 and gives a 20% chance to ignore enemy Weapon Defense. The ignore proc helps more against high-WDEF mobs and cannot be part of a guaranteed low-roll kill.

Put one point in Final Attack at level 33 and leave it on while you fight single mobs. Lv1 has a 20% chance to add a 220% hit, and Final Attack costs no MP. With Arrow Blow or Double Shot, that is about 18% more damage per MP. Each proc uses up 1 arrow.

Each FA proc replays your crossbow shot as its own attack animation, and you can't attack again until it ends: about 0.8 seconds with Booster. At Lv1, your average damage per second on one mob drops by about 1%, and you drink fewer MP potions.
Final Attack: Crossbow only hits 1 mob. Once Iron Arrow is maxed and reaches two or more mobs, the extra animation costs more damage than the proc adds.

Max Final Attack has a 50% chance to add a 250% single-target hit. The Hunter version fires three 90% arrows instead. Grummash's build stops at Lv11, a 30% chance for 230% damage: about 29 % more damage per MP against one mob. Levels 2-11 come last because each one raises that bonus by only about 1 percentage point. blocks.h2: Find Your Build's Best Training Map with Training Advisor

blocks.p: **Danger measures how hard a mob hits you for: under 10% of your HP is Safe, 10-24% is Caution, 25-49% is Danger, and 50%+ is Lethal.**
A map with four clean targets can beat a higher-level map where Iron Arrow only reaches one or two. Run the check with your crossbow and the platforms you can actually hold.

ol: Enter the Crossbowman's AP, equipment, scrolls, arrow stack, skills, and active buffs.
Choose Iron Arrow when mobs stand lined up in front of you, or Double Shot when most pulls are single target.
Set reliability to 100% and leave Factor Danger into recommendations enabled.
Check the guaranteed attack count for every common spawn, including lower-EXP mobs.
Open the map page and confirm its lanes are long enough for all four piercing targets.

Check the nearest potion and arrow shops. A nearest-town scroll gets you back to town, but the long walk back to the map can erase an Iron Arrow map's EXP advantage. Soul Arrow reduces arrow trips once its uptime feels comfortable.

ol: **Reading 180% as 180% on all four mobs.** Iron Arrow falls to 80%, 60%, and 40% of the first target's damage.
**Using a bow after spending Crossbowman SP.** Mastery, Booster, Final Attack, Soul Arrow, and Iron Arrow require a crossbow.
**Ignoring platform direction.** Iron Arrow needs mobs lined up in front. A vertically stacked map can waste most of its cap.

**Forgetting whack range.** Leave at least 65 px between you and the nearest mob. Your crossbow whacks at close range by design, and Power Knockback is a first-job skill for pushing mobs back out of it.
**Adding Hunter-level STR.** The level 70 Crossbowman weapon needs 60 STR. The saved build puts the next ten AP into DEX.
